_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); railroad signals

pit_profile.why: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not

classification.quality_note: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.82x; +28% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.05; conservative 2yr -0%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -29.0%/yr (worst year FY99-FY07, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.1%/yr (Q4 2007 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 9.2-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +10.8%/yr (FY99-FY07 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +43.0%/yr (best 2-yr run FY99-FY07); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: UNP (retrospective, 2008-04-04) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 1.82x (61.8% downside to Bear $51 / +33.9% upside to Bull $179) | Adj composite 2.58 vs market 2.63: gap -0.05 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +29% above the EPP floor $104 (13x FY08E $8.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: -0.1% total (-0.0%/yr) | At 16.7x FY08E the 15% hurdle price $177 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; carloads +0% in Q4 2007, forward revenue +6% (no FY08 revenue guide, Q4 2007 commodity revenue); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2007 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2003-2007; 2007 diluted shares 268.4M, effective tax rate 38.4%, interest expense $482M, other income $116M; 2008 Outlook: earnings of $7.75 to $8.25 per diluted share, volume within a range of 1% higher to 1% lower than 2007, fuel prices 15% to 20% above the 2007 average, record revenue and an improved operating ratio in words; capital investments of about $3.1 billion

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2006 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2002-2006 (operating revenue, diluted EPS from continuing operations, operating margin and ratio, carloads); 2006 diluted shares 272.0M, effective tax rate 36.4%, interest expense $477M, other income $118M; competition (BNSF parallel routes); 2007 Outlook: commodity revenue growth target 6% to 7%, volume growth 2% to 3%, earnings growth of 10% to 15% and an operating ratio below 80%; quarterly dividend raised to $0.35 on 2007-01-30; 20M-share repurchase authorized 2007-01-30 through 2009

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2004 10-K
sources.supports: ten-year selected financial data 1995-2004 on the continuing-operations basis (trucking reclassified as discontinued): 1998 loss from continuing operations ($0.41 per diluted share), 1999 $3.05, 2000 $3.22 (includes a $72M after-tax work force reduction charge); operating revenue 1999 $10,175M, 2000 $10,765M

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2005 10-K
sources.supports: selected financial data 2001-2005: 2001 diluted EPS from continuing operations $3.65, operating revenues $10,830M

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation FY2001 10-K
sources.supports: 1999 weighted-average diluted shares 269.8M (earnings per share note)

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q4 2005 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: company-published EPS excluding one-offs: 2004 $2.89 per diluted share excluding the non-cash asbestos charge ($2.30 reported), 2005 $3.41 excluding the income tax expense reduction ($3.85 reported)

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation Q4 2007 results (8-K ex.99.1)
sources.supports: Q4 and full-year 2007 revenue detail by commodity group (revenue, carloads, average revenue per car), operating ratio, GTMs per employee, diluted EPS ($6.91 for 2007) and shares, effective tax rate, cash, free cash flow, share repurchases (12.6M in 2007, 63% of the 20M program); 2008 outlook in words only ('post another record year in 2008')
